Gunturu Bhaskar Rao vs Venigalla Surya Prakasa Rao Died on 4
September, 2025
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice Battu Devanand
 Civil Revision Petition NOs.2196 And 2197 Of 2025
Common Order:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
-
These Civil Revision Petitions have been filed against the common order, dated 23.06.2025 in I.A.No.41 of 2025 and I.A.No.42 of 2025 in O.S.No.381 of 2016 on the file of Principal Civil Judge (Junior Division), Mangalagiri.
2. Petitioner herein is Plaintiff No.8 in the suit filed for declaration of title.

The plaintiffs in the suit filed a petition vide I.A.No.41 of 2025 seeking to re-open the evidence of the plaintiffs for the purpose of summoning the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri for producing the relevant file and to depose on behalf of the plaintiffs.

I.A.No.42 of 2025 is filed seeking to summon the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri Mandal to produce the record and to give evidence with regard to lodging criminal complaint in Crime No.40 of 2016, dated 25.02.2016 before the Mangalagiri Rural Police Station against the 2nd defendant in the suit.
3. The 2nd defendant/2nd respondent herein filed counter refuting the request made by the plaintiffs in two Interlocutory Applications.

4. The case of the petitioner herein is that the suit schedule property was purchased by one Kolavennu Peraiah, S/o.Kotaiah, his great grandfather by virtue of registered Sale Deed No.683,
dated 23.05.1916.
They came to know that the 2nd respondent had sold the suit schedule property to 1st respondent under registered sale deed No.5874, dated 12.08.2015.

As per the recitals of the said document, the property was the ancestral property of the 2nd respondent and he had pattadar passbook and land ownership title deed book issued by Mangalagiri Revenue authority in his favour.
But, originally the property was in possession and enjoyment of the plaintiffs.
As per the plaintiff/petitioner, the sale deed between Respondent Nos.1 and 2 is sham and collusive.
Having knowledge about the same, the plaintiffs have lodged a complaint before the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri and they have also made several representations to the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri.

Finally, the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri lodged a criminal complaint against the 2nd respondent before the Mangalagiri Rural Police Station and a case in Crime No.40 of 2016, dated 25.02.2016 under Sections 420, 468, 471 of IPC was registered.
The then Tahsildar, Mangalagiri gave statement that Gunturu Bhaskar Rao vs Venigalla Surya Prakasa Rao Died on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136408017/

entities.text: Gunturu Bhaskar Rao vs Venigalla Surya Prakasa Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 the 2 nd respondent had fabricated and concocted the pattadar passbook, land ownership rights book by forging the signatures of the concerned authorities in connivance with Village Revenue Officers.
5. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that if the 2 nd respondent entered into witness box, all these facts would have come to light in his evidence.
But the 2nd respondent had not chosen to adduce any evidence on his behalf and thereby the evidence on behalf of the respondents was closed.
As such, the plaintiffs lost the opportunity to cross-examine the 2nd respondent.

Under those circumstances, as the plaintiffs have no other option except to summon the Tahsildar,
Mangalagiri to give evidence on the fact of lodging criminal complaint against the 2nd defendant,
the plaintiffs prayed to re-open the evidence on behalf of the plaintiffs to summon Tahsildar,
Mangalagiri to produce the relevant file and to give evidence.

6. In the counter affidavit filed by the 2nd defendant/2nd respondent in the trial Court it is averred that the plaintiffs got knowledge about the alleged case details in Crime No.40 of 2016 of Mangalagiri Rural Police Station and they got opportunity to obtain certified copies of the same from the concerned Court or from the concerned police.
Hence, they ought to have produce the same before the Court at the time of adducing evidence on behalf of the plaintiffs.

But, with a view to drag on the proceedings, the plaintiffs by abusing the process of law got filed the present petitions with false, baseless and vexatious allegations, for which they are not entitled.

7. Having considered the contentions of the respective parties, the trial Court opined that as the certified copy of the FIR along with the remand report of the 2nd accused/2nd defendant was got marked as Ex.A4, no useful purpose would be served in summoning the present Tahsildar,
Mangalagiri Rural.
Accordingly, the trial Court held that the plaintiffs are not entitled for any relief and accordingly, dismissed the two (2) Interlocutory Applications, vide Common order, dated 23.06.2025.
Aggrieved by the said common order, the present Civil Revision Petitions are filed.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the trial Court erroneously dismissed the Interlocutory Applications filed by the plaintiffs to reopen the plaintiffs' evidence and to summon the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri for production of documents pertaining to the suit schedule property without any valid reasons.

The learned counsel further contends that the main purpose of summoning the Tahsildar is to give evidence with regard to lodging criminal complaint in Crime No.40 of 2016 of Mangalagiri Rural Police Station as he is the author of the said complaint.

In view of the non-examination of the witness on behalf of the respondents/defendants, the only opportunity left to the plaintiffs to prove Ex.A4 is by examining the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri as witness on behalf of them.

He further contends that no prejudice will be caused to the respondents if the Tahsildar, Mangalagiri is examined and prayed to set aside the common order, dated 23.06.2025 passed in I.A.No.41 of 2025 and I.A.No.42 of 2025 in O.S.No.381 of 2016.

9. Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and upon careful examination of the material available on record, it is an admitted fact that the evidence of the plaintiffs was closed on 15.10.2024 and defendant's side evidence was closed as 'no evidence' on 23.12.2024.

Since then, the matter underwent several adjournments till 21.01.2025 and number of Gunturu Bhaskar Rao vs Venigalla Surya Prakasa Rao Died on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136408017/

sentences.text: 2 conditional orders were imposed.

In view of the fact that the F.I.R lodged by the Mangalagiri Rural police in Crime No.40 of 2016 against the 2nd respondent/2nd defendant basing on the complaint made by the then Tahsildar, Mangalagiri was got marked as Ex.A4, in our considered view no useful purpose would be served by summoning the present Tahsildar, Mangalagiri Rural.

The same view was expressed by the trial Court while dismissing the two (02) Interlocutory applications.
10.

In view of the same, in our considered view, there is no irregularity or infirmity in the common order passed by the learned trial Court dismissing the two (02) Interlocutory Applications and this Court is not inclined to interfere into the said common order.
11. Accordingly, the Civil Revision Petitions are dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in these cases shall stand closed.
